title: FormAct: Agentic Source Editing for Rich-Format Document Generation
one_liner: Generate polished documents by letting one agent edit source files and another agent review rendered pages across several repair rounds.
lead: Producing a polished document is more than producing text. The system has to manage layout, structure, and formatting errors that only become obvious after rendering the page. FormAct addresses this by working on the source representation directly and by separating editing from review. One agent changes the HTML source with tools, while another agent inspects the rendered result and points out what still needs to change. The loop helps because visual defects often cannot be judged from source text alone.

problem.h2: Why document generation needs more than one pass of text output
paras: A professional document has structure, spacing, headings, and visual consistency. A single direct generation step often leaves broken layout or malformed source because the model cannot fully judge the final appearance before rendering.

This creates a two-view problem. The editor needs to reason about source code, while the reviewer needs to reason about the rendered page. If one system handles both views poorly, defects can persist because the source may look acceptable while the page still looks wrong.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Treat document generation as iterative source editing with tools and rendered-page review so that each round can fix issues exposed by the previous render.

panels.title: 1. Start from a document request
panels.viz_args: The system receives a request for a polished document
panels.caption: The request includes content goals, but the final page also needs acceptable structure and appearance.

panels.title: 2. The editing agent writes source
panels.viz_args: It edits HTML with help from source-aware tools
panels.caption: Working at the source level makes repairs explicit and easier to track.

panels.title: 3. The page is rendered and reviewed
panels.caption: Rendering exposes defects that source text alone may hide.

panels.title: 4. Feedback guides another edit round
panels.viz_args: Reviewer comments tell the editor what to repair next
panels.caption: The loop continues because each round narrows the gap between request and final page.

panels.title: 5. The document stabilizes
panels.caption: The final output has fewer formatting errors because source edits were judged against rendered evidence.

steps.text: Work on HTML rather than raw final text so that structure and formatting can be edited directly.
Give the editor a source-aware editor and a template retriever because those tools make structural changes easier to execute correctly.
Turn the source into a visible page so that actual appearance can be inspected.
Let a second agent critique visible defects because many layout problems only appear after rendering.
Shorten the working history after each edit trigger so that long repair sessions stay manageable.

paras: The paper changes document generation from one-shot writing into a source-and-review loop. It makes rendering part of the reasoning process because the document should be judged in the same form that readers will see.
object.object: the iterative document state made of source, render, and reviewer feedback

hidden.name: the gap between the current source and the page the user actually wants
paras: The key hidden quantity is the remaining mismatch between the present source and the desired final document. The model cannot read that mismatch directly from the request after many edit rounds because the important errors are distributed across source structure and rendered appearance.

The reviewer exposes that hidden gap by inspecting the rendered page. A render may reveal broken spacing, weak hierarchy, or missing sections, and those observations tell the editor which part of the source still needs to change.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark hidden mismatches that review feedback can surface clearly after rendering.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is what is still wrong about the current document even if the source looks mostly plausible.
The editing and review loop matters because rendering makes that hidden mismatch easier to observe and repair.

mechanism.h2: Why this works: source edits need rendered feedback
paras: Direct document generation often fails because the model commits to a large output before it has evidence about how that output renders. Once the page is rendered, however, visible defects can be named and repaired one by one.

FormAct exploits that structure by separating roles. The editor focuses on changing source correctly with tools, while the reviewer focuses on judging the rendered page. This division helps because each role gets feedback in the form it can use best, and the repeated loop steadily reduces page defects.

stages.s: Document request plus current HTML source
Editor changes the source with tools
Render the page and inspect the result
Reviewer returns repair guidance because the render exposed visible issues
A cleaner final document after several repair rounds

math.h2: Choose edits that improve the rendered page
math.words: A simple summary is to score each edit round by combining source correctness and rendered-page quality. The system keeps refining while the score can still increase.
symbols: overall quality of one edit-review round
how correct and well-structured the HTML source is after the edit
how acceptable the visible rendered page is after review
weight on the rendered-page part of the score

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Round A fixes the HTML tags but leaves poor spacing in the rendered page.
Its source quality is 8 and its render quality is 3, so with gamma equal to 1 the total score is 11.
Round B keeps the source correct and also fixes the spacing.
Its source quality is 8 and its render quality is 6, so the total score is 14.
The later round is better because the visible page improved while source correctness was preserved.

math.note: The paper uses a fuller system than this equation, but the score captures the main principle that source edits should be judged by rendered results too.

charts.title: Direct or weaker baselines
charts.note: Baselines struggle because they lack the same edit-review loop over rendered evidence.

charts.title: FormAct
charts.note: The paper reports stronger document quality because iterative source editing and rendered review catch issues that one-pass generation misses.

items.b: A reviewer can point to symptoms but miss the source cause.
items.html: The rendered page may reveal that something is wrong without revealing which source block caused it, so repair rounds can still wander.

items.b: Context compression can hide earlier intent.
items.html: If the system shortens history too aggressively, later edits may forget why a section was written in a certain way because the original constraint is no longer visible.

items.b: Template retrieval can steer style too strongly.
items.html: A fetched template may dominate the output and weaken task-specific structure because the editor copies more than it should.
The framework is useful because it treats document quality as something that emerges through edit and review, not as something guaranteed by the first draft.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small document generator that writes HTML for a report, renders it in a browser, and then sends a screenshot plus the source to a reviewer module. Let the reviewer request repairs such as heading hierarchy fixes, spacing fixes, or missing-section fixes.
The demo should track whether each review round reduces visible defects. It should show that the loop improves output because the system can act on source while judging the result in rendered form.
demo.metric_eq: repair_gain = defect_count_start - defect_count_end ; review_hit_rate = accepted_review_fixes / total_review_fixes
demo.closing: The point is to make visible why rendered review changes the quality of source-based document generation.
